name: TheTop
summary: An enterprise layer in front of your AI providers: it attributes spend by department, reuses repeated work, routes each task to a cheaper model and applies policy before execution. Self-serve entry at $175 a month for the first 12 months (then $350), with usage-based pricing beyond it (pricing page read 23 Nov 2026).
best_for: enterprises running AI across several departments, models and applications that cannot answer what the bill bought: organisations with a real AI invoice to explain, a CFO asking for return per team, and a security function that wants oversight without reading employees' conversations
skip_if: you are one person or a small team looking for an assistant: this is no longer that product. The $8 morning-brief tool this page used to describe has been withdrawn. The cheapest way in is now a $175-a-month package (rising to $350 after a year) that reports and polices company AI spend across provider keys, which only makes sense if you have an AI bill worth explaining
honest_knock:
The price is public now, but the bill is hard to predict past the launch package. Transparency moves between $150 and $500 a month with your AI spend, Governance is metered per million tokens, and Optimization is a percentage of routed spend in brackets. The $175 entry is a 12-month launch price that becomes $350 a month.

The savings are measured by the vendor, against a baseline the vendor computes. The Optimization fee is capped at measured savings, which protects you from paying more than you save on TheTop's own numbers, not on yours. Ask how the baseline is defined, which traffic counts, and whether you can audit the calculation: a reroute that swaps a frontier model for a cheaper one also changes the output, and only your own evaluation shows whether that trade was worth it.

This product sits in the request path. Memory, caching, routing and policy are applied before traffic reaches the model, which is where the savings come from and also where an outage or a bad routing rule lands on every AI feature you run. Starting read-only is the right shape, but the day you point production at it, a middle layer has become a dependency.

pricing.notes:
(read 23 November 2026 on thetop.com/pricing) TheTop publishes prices again. On 19 September 2026 that URL returned a 404 and every button said Book a demo; it now carries a full rate card, priced on your AI spend and on the tokens that pass through TheTop.

The one self-serve product is a launch offer: Transparency plus Governance in one package for $175 a month for your first 12 months, then $350 a month. Billed monthly, cancel anytime, prices in USD excluding taxes. There is no free trial; the page says you connect a read-only key and see your last 30 days of AI spend before you pay.

The full card, as published: Transparency costs $150 to $500 a month depending on your AI spend (measured on the keys you connect over the trailing 30 days), with up to 5 logins per organization at every band. Governance is $0.50 per million tokens checked on the first billion a month, falling to $0.15 above 200 billion, and never more than 10% of your AI spend; Transparency is included once the Governance fee reaches $150 a month. Optimization takes a share of the AI spend routed through TheEngine, in marginal brackets: 7% on the first $50K a month, 5% from $50K to $100K, 2.5% from $100K to $500K, 2.25% from $500K to $2M and 1.5% above $2M. That fee is capped at the savings TheEngine measures that month. The Complete Package (Governance plus Optimization) takes 15% off and includes Transparency; annual agreements are available only there. Optimization and the Complete Package are set up with their team.

The page's own worked examples: at $200K a month of Sonnet-led spend, about 32B tokens, Governance comes to $9,150 and Optimization to $8,500. The savings percentage in their estimator is your own assumption; the page says so itself.

The $8 a month and $80 a year an older version of this review quoted belonged to the previous product, a personal assistant, and cannot be bought today. The large dollar figures on the home page ($34,800.25 spent, $30,667.06 saved) sit inside a dashboard mock-up and are not prices.

compare_with.name: LangSmith
compare_with.why: Both sit between your teams and the models, but they are sold to different buyers. LangSmith is developer tooling for tracing, evaluating and debugging LLM applications, with published per-seat and usage pricing you can start on your own. TheTop is an enterprise layer pitched at the CFO, the Head of AI and the CISO together: spend attribution by department, policy before execution, sensitive-data detection in stream, and reuse and routing meant to lower the bill: with a $175-a-month self-serve entry and usage-based pricing beyond it (read 23 November 2026). If you want to debug your own agents, LangSmith is the cheaper and faster answer; if you need to explain a six-figure AI invoice to finance, that is the question TheTop is built for.
